source_refs.note: Exercise 5.1 (book p. 154), Question 11; answer key PDF 306 (Answers 5.1, key numbered 14).

blocks.prompt: 11. Find the condition that the lines \(y = m_1x + c_1\); \(y = m_2x + c_2\) and \(y = m_3x + c_3\) are concurrent.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh Theorem 3 ka aam (sirf letters wala) roop hai; koi number nahi, poora formula nikalna hai.
Lines slope-intercept form mein di hui hain, jab ke Theorem 3 general form maangta hai.
Is liye pehle har line ko \(ax + by + c = 0\) mein badlenge.
Plan: general form, determinant, expand, aur saaf tarteeb.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = m_ix + c_i\), \(i = 1, 2, 3\).
Maloom karna: concurrency ki shart.
Tareeqa: har line ko general form mein likh kar Theorem 3 lagana.

General form
\[m_1x - y + c_1 = 0\]
\[m_2x - y + c_2 = 0\]
\[m_3x - y + c_3 = 0\]
Kyun: Theorem 3 \(ax + by + c = 0\) wali shakal maangta hai; yahan \(a = m_i\), \(b = -1\), \(c = c_i\).
Dhyan dein: \(b = -1\) hai, \(+1\) nahi, kyunke \(y\) ko left side laye to sign badal gaya.

Theorem 3 (alag slopes wali lines)
\[\begin{vmatrix} m_1 & -1 & c_1 \\ m_2 & -1 & c_2 \\ m_3 & -1 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
Kyun: slopes \(m_1, m_2, m_3\) alag hon to lines parallel nahi, aur Theorem 3 lag sakta hai.

Saaf tarteeb
\[m_1(c_2 - c_3) + m_2(c_3 - c_1)\]
\[+ m_3(c_1 - c_2) = 0\]
Kyun: har \(m_i\) ke terms ikatthe kiye; yeh wohi chhe terms hain jo answer key mein \(m_1c_2 - m_2c_1 + m_2c_3 - m_3c_2 + m_3c_1 - m_1c_3 = 0\) likhe hain, sirf tarteeb alag hai.
Is shart ko yaad rakhne ka aasaan tareeqa: \(m_1, m_2, m_3\) aur \(c_1, c_2, c_3\) ko ek chakkar (cycle) mein socho; har \(m\) ke saath baqi do \(c\) ka farq aata hai.

Tasdeeq (doosra tareeqa):
Line 1 aur 2 wahan milti hain jahan \(m_1x + c_1 = m_2x + c_2\), yani \(x = \frac{c_2 - c_1}{m_1 - m_2}\), \(y = \frac{m_1c_2 - m_2c_1}{m_1 - m_2}\). Yeh point \(y = m_3x + c_3\) mein rakh kar \(m_1 - m_2\) se multiply karein: \(m_1c_2 - m_2c_1 = m_3(c_2 - c_1) + c_3(m_1 - m_2)\), jo tarteeb badalne par wohi shart hai. Misaal: \(y = x\), \(y = 2x - 1\), \(y = 3x - 2\) teeno \((1, 1)\) se guzarti hain, aur \(1(-1 + 2) + 2(-2 - 0) + 3(0 + 1) = 1 - 4 + 3 = 0\).
